name: Small Garden, Big Impact
purpose: At Johnson Hills Park, Lucy created eight micro-gardens with 62 native pollinator plants, showing visitors that even one or two native plants can make a meaningful difference.

chapters.title: A garden anyone could imagine
chapters.body: Lucy designed the project around a simple idea: helping pollinators should feel possible for everyone. Rather than one large display garden, she planned small native-plant groupings around the park to demonstrate how a home garden of any size can support biodiversity.
chapters.alt: Native plants arranged in their planned locations around one of the garden beds
chapters.caption: Planning the micro-gardens

chapters.title: Turning a plan into support
chapters.body: She built a detailed task chart, raised $2,250 through an online campaign, a restaurant fundraiser, neighborhood outreach, and the Anderson Township Pollinator Committee's Native Plant Initiative. Native Roots discounted the plants, while Trauth Landscaping donated part of the mulch and delivered it.
chapters.alt: Lucy selecting plants at a local garden center
chapters.caption: Selecting plants for the project

chapters.title: Leading through delegation
chapters.body: Lucy divided volunteers into patrols, briefed each patrol leader, and delegated work through them. The structure let her coordinate 41 people across several small planting sites while staying focused on safety, questions, and the bigger picture instead of doing every task herself.
chapters.alt: Lucy holding her project binder while volunteers work behind her
chapters.caption: Directing the work crews

chapters.title: Adapting in the rain
chapters.body: Cold, wet weather required canopies and extra care to keep everyone safe. More volunteers arrived than expected, the planting areas became crowded, and the mulch delivery ran late. Lucy adjusted assignments, kept the groups moving, and stayed positive when the day did not follow the plan.
chapters.alt: Volunteers spreading mulch and working in the gardens around the manor
chapters.caption: Building together despite the weather

chapters.title: A living lesson in impact
chapters.body: The completed project added eight micro-gardens and 62 native pollinator plants to Johnson Hills Park. The gardens bring color and biodiversity to the park, but their larger purpose is educational: each planting shows that a small patch of native plants can become part of a much bigger environmental impact.
chapters.alt: The completed native pollinator gardens surrounding the historic manor
chapters.caption: Eight gardens, one shared impact
